subject: Cost sensitivity & route addition — Nutrify post-call recap
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@nutrify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cost sensitivity & route addition — post-call recap

Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

What we heard
- Primary ask: clear unit economics for your generation and embeddings workloads once you add the 16k-context model and a separate embeddings route.
- Current target (from internal budget): ~10M committed tokens / month initially, ramp to 40–50M over 3 quarters if quality holds.
- Procurement wants a target blended cost to model into the renewal (target $/1M tokens).

High-level proposal (straw man attached)
- Committed baseline: 10M tokens / month. If Nutrify commits to 10M/mo for 12 months, proposed starting effective rate = $12.50 / 1M tokens for generation routes.
- Embeddings route: lower unit cost given smaller model and batched throughput — proposed $3.75 / 1M embedding tokens when routed separately.
- Step-up schedule: Q1: 10M, Q2: 25M, Q3: 40M — we'll build blended pricing so your effective $/1M declines as you add volume and the embeddings route.
- Blended rate mechanics: per-route metering with quarterly reconciliation and an invoice-level blended credit applied when volume thresholds are hit. Details in attached PDF.

Questions / asks for you
1) Please confirm the budget range Nutrify expects for the renewal (ballpark $/1M target or monthly $ cap).
2) Who is the procurement contact for PO/contract timeline (CC'd procurement@nutrify.ai if available)?
3) Any required compliance docs for the legal team — we can start pulling SOC2/Audit artifacts once you confirm the procurement timeline.

Next steps
- I'll loop in Ben to propose concrete blended tables and a 3-tier step-up schedule by EOD Monday.
- You review the attached straw-man pricing + the usage projection CSV and tell us if the ramp looks realistic.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0193

Attachments: Nutrify_Proposed_Tiered_Pricing_v1.pdf (proposal), nutritify_usage_projection_Q1-Q4.csv (est. volumes)
From: Laura Chen <laura@nutrify.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: James Park <james.park@nutrify.ai>, procurement@nutrify.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cost sensitivity & route addition — post-call recap

Evelyn — thanks for the clear write-up and for joining the call. Quick answers below and a couple of clarifications:

Budget & target
- Our finance lead is modeling a target blended spend around $9k–$13k / 1M tokens (we're trying to hit sub-$12k if possible with volume). That band is what we'd consider for center-of-budget conversations.
- Initial commitment we can get to: 12M tokens / month for the first 3 months, with an expected ramp to ~35M/mo by the end of Q2 (subject to quality/regression testing).

Routes & models
- We'll definitely want a dedicated embeddings route. Embeddings volume is likely to be ~15–20% of overall token count but more latency-tolerant.
- The 16k-context generation model will be used for a subset of traffic (approx 25% initially) — happy to discuss how that impacts blended math.

Procurement
- procurement@nutrify.ai is the right inbox; our procurement manager is Priya Singh. Please include a formal quote/attachment we can circulate.

Can Ben send a couple of blended-scenario tables that show: (a) blended $/1M at the 12M/35M/50M breakpoints, and (b) line-item generation vs embeddings pricing? If you can show a conservative and an aggressive ramp, that would help our CFO.

—Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Platform, Nutrify Inc.
laura@nutrify.ai | +1 617-555-0128
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Cost sensitivity & route addition — straw blended scenarios (internal)

Eve / Priyom — moving the pricing details into the thread so Nutrify sees one coherent doc. Below are three quick scenarios (high level, exact numbers in attached PDF):

Scenario A — Conservative ramp (12M -> 20M)
- Generation: $13.25 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings: $4.10 / 1M tokens
- Effective blended (weighted by expected route split): ~$10.95 / 1M tokens

Scenario B — Base case (12M -> 35M)
- Generation: $12.00 / 1M tokens (applies up to 25M)
- Generation (volume above 25M): $9.50 / 1M tokens
- Embeddings: $3.75 / 1M tokens
- Blended effective: ~$9.85 / 1M tokens at 35M with 20% embed share

Scenario C — Aggressive ramp (12M -> 50M)
- Generation tiering: $11.00 / 1M up to 30M, $8.75 / 1M beyond 30M
- Embeddings: $3.25 / 1M
- Blended effective: ~$8.50 / 1M tokens at 50M with 18% embed share

Other notes
- We recommend a quarterly reconciliation and a crediting mechanism rather than retroactive invoices to keep cashflow simple for the customer.
- We should offer a contractual route-addition clause: adding a new route (like embeddings) triggers an initial 30-day trial pricing window; final blended credits apply at quarter end when volumes stabilize.
- Priyom: can you confirm capacity (burst + reserved) implications for the 16k model and whether we need to price burst separately? If yes, add a small per-GB memory premium in the next draft.

I'll attach the detailed table (Nutrify_Proposed_Tiered_Pricing_v1.pdf) and the usage projection. Happy to tweak numbers — want to keep us competitive while protecting unit economics.

—Ben

Subject: Re: Cost sensitivity & route addition — next steps and pricing review call

Laura — thanks, that budget band is super helpful. Proposed next steps to get to a PO quickly:

1) Pricing review call: Ben and I can walk through Scenario B vs C on Monday (Nov 2) at 10:00am PT. Can you confirm if that works for Priya?
2) Draft quote: Ben will circulate a one-page quote (attaching the PDF in this thread) that Procurement can use to raise an initial PO.
3) Contract addendum: we will include a short amendment that documents the embeddings route addition window (30-day test), quarterly reconciliation rules, and the step-up tiers. Legal can draft once you confirm the PO timing.

Operational note for Nutrify: If you need hard SLAs for the 16k route we should discuss Dedicated pool vs hosted fallbacks; Priyom, can you prepare an estimate for dedicated capacity and a brief note on fallback latency/throughput?

I'll hold Monday 10am PT. If we don't hear back from Procurement by EOD Monday we'll follow up via the procurement inbox.

Best,
Evelyn
